identity.title: Multiple Outflows in the High-mass Cluster-forming Region G25.82-0.17

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present results of continuum and spectral line observations with ALMA and 22 GHz water (H$_2$O) maser observations using KaVA and VERA toward a high-mass star-forming region, G25.82–0.17.

question.value: What are the evolutionary stages, outflows, disk/rotation and mass of the YSOs in the high-mass cluster-forming region G25.82-0.17, and does it support turbulent core accretion?

evidence.quote: To investigate the mechanism of high-mass star formation in the G25.82 region, we carried out 1.3 mm continuum and spectral line observations with ALMA and 22 GHz H$_2$O maser observations using KaVA and VERA.

method.value: 2D Gaussian fits to emission >10 sigma in 1.3 mm continuum

analysis_steps.goal: Measure line parameters and outflow maps

method.value: Robust Gaussian fits to line profiles; integrated intensity maps over blue/red velocity ranges for SiO

evidence.quote: Using a Gaussian profile, robust fitting was done to derive line parameters such as the peak flux density, central velocity, and full width half maximum (FWHM) of the Gaussian.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive total mass from dust continuum

method.value: Optically thin graybody M = S D^2/(kappa B(Tdust))

evidence.quote: Assuming the emission is optically thin graybody radiation, we can derive the total enclosed mass (gas+dust)

assumptions.value: Tdust = 150 K (75-300 K); D = 5.0 kpc; kappa=0.1(250um/lambda)^beta cm2/g, beta=1.85; gas-to-dust 100; starless cores at 15 K

evidence.quote: dust temperature ($T_{\textrm{dust}}$) is assumed to be 150 K with an uncertainty by a factor of 2 (75 K - 300 K).

findings_qualitative.value: Two SiO outflows (N–S and SE–NW); N–S driven by G25.82-W1, SE–NW driver uncertain

evidence.quote: The driving source of the N–S SiO outflow is G25.82–W1 while that of the SE–NW SiO outflow is uncertain.

claims.hypothesis: Is G25.82-W1 a high-mass YSO with a rotating structure?
claims.experiment: Continuum mass and Keplerian estimate from CH3OH 22_4-21_5 velocity gradient
claims.result: Total mass 20-84 Msun; dynamical mass 25±11 Msun lower limit
claims.finding: G25.82-W1 is a HM-YSO with rotating disk or envelope

evidence.quote: Thus, G25.82–W1 appears to be a HM-YSO surrounded by a rotating disk or envelope.

claims.experiment: SiO 5-4 integrated maps and H2O masers
claims.result: Two SiO outflows plus an H2O maser outflow with inconsistent velocity structure
claims.finding: Multiple outflows from a cluster-forming region

evidence.quote: Given the multiple outflows and multiple sources, G25.82 is a high-mass cluster formation.

claims.hypothesis: Do high-mass stars form in individual high-mass cores (turbulent core accretion)?
claims.experiment: Search for low-mass cores in 1.3 mm continuum
claims.result: No low-mass cores detected at 5 sigma ~2 mJy/beam (~0.5 Msun)
claims.finding: Consistent with scaled-up low-mass formation, unresolved cores not excluded

evidence.quote: Our results do not show the presence of a cluster of low-mass cores around the detected three high-mass cores

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: H2O maser outflow could be a separate small-scale outflow or the inner part of the N–S SiO outflow

evidence.quote: However, we cannot rule out the possibility that the H$_2$O maser outflow is tracing the inner part of the large scale outflow (N–S SiO outflow).

limitations_admitted.value: Dynamical mass is a lower limit because inclination is unknown

evidence.quote: Our mass estimate is a lower limit because the inclination of the disk is unknown.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dynamical mass from a crude R v^2/G with a 3 km/s velocity difference at ~2.6 km/s channels is poorly constrained
Assumed Tdust of 150 K drives the mass range
The non-detection of low-mass cores at 0.25" resolution does not rule out unresolved cores
Class I maser vs thermal CH3OH interpretation is qualitative
